title: ZIP local file header
summary: Each file in a ZIP archive begins with a 30-byte (minimum) local file header: signature 0x04034B50, version needed, flags, compression method, modtime, CRC-32, compressed/uncompressed sizes, filename length, extra field length, then the filename and extra field, then the (possibly compressed) file data.

ext.summary: Each file in a ZIP archive begins with a 30-byte (minimum) local file header: signature 0x04034B50, version needed, flags, compression method, modtime, CRC-32, compressed/uncompressed sizes, filename length, extra field length, then the filename and extra field, then the (possibly compressed) file data.

structure.meaning: Minimum PKZIP version to extract (e.g. 20 = 2.0, 45 = 4.5 with ZIP64).
Bit 0 = encrypted, bit 3 = data descriptor follows, bit 11 = UTF-8 filename, ... .
CRC-32 of uncompressed data (0 if data descriptor used).
Size of compressed data (0 if data descriptor used).
Size of uncompressed data (0 if data descriptor used).
Length of the filename that follows.
Length of the extra field that follows.
The file's path/name (UTF-8 if flag bit 11 set).
Tagged extra data blocks (ZIP64, Unix uid/gid, NTFS timestamps, ...).

ext.example_decoded: Local header for 'hello.txt', stored (method 0), empty extra
notes: Central directory entries (0x02014B50) at the end of the archive list every file with offsets.
End of central directory record (0x06054B50) gives the offset to the central directory.
ZIP64 (version 4.5) uses 0xFFFFFFFF sentinels and an extra field for large sizes.
Data descriptor (flag bit 3) is used when CRC/size are not known before compression (streaming).
